correctness.rationale: The infinite convolution has product mask (1+Σ_i e^(2πim_i/b^j))/4 with summable factor deviations; nonzero factors give a nonzero product. Four unit vectors sum to zero only in opposite pairs; since one term is 1, for even b a zero occurs at a level iff one coordinate is b^j/2 mod b^j and the two remaining coordinates differ by b^j/2; odd b has no zeros. The two live residue patterns A=(0,0,0) and B_i=(0,u,u), u≠0, encode all possible future zeros. Transition recurrences produce G_b(z)=3z((b-1)b²-z)/[(b³-z)(b²-z)] and q_{b,j}=3/(b-1)[b^(-3j)+(b-2)b^(-2j)]. A cancellation from B is terminal, and from A can leave B only, so at most two levels, with double density 3/[(b³-1)(b²-1)]. The late-level event is bounded by (1+3(b^L-1))/b^(3L), validating natural densities. Independently enumerated congruence cancellations for (b,L)=(2,4),(4,3),(6,2): first-level counts (1536,192,24,3), (36864,2112,129), (3240,87); b=4 double count 828 of 262144. Finite checks corroborate but do not prove all b,L.
